requirement: An airline company owns multiple airplanes, each with an Airplane Number, Model, and Passenger Capacity. Each airplane can perform many flights. Each flight has a Flight Number, Departure Time, Arrival Time, Origin, and Destination, and is operated by exactly one airplane.

A warehousing company manages multiple warehouses, each with a Warehouse Number, Address, and Capacity. There are many goods, each with a Goods ID and Goods Name. Each inbound or outbound transaction records a Transaction ID, Time, Transaction Type, and the warehouse involved; a transaction can move many goods, and for each good the Quantity is recorded.

A company manages employees and the departments they work in. Each department has a Department ID, Name, and Budget. Each employee has an Employee ID, Name, Hire Date, and Salary, and works in exactly one department. A department can have many employees.

A hotel manages rooms and guest reservations. Each room has a Room Number, Room Type, and Rate. Each guest has a Guest ID, Name, and Phone Number. A reservation has a Reservation ID, Check-in Date, and Check-out Date; each reservation is made by one guest for one room. A guest can make many reservations.

A telecom provider offers service plans to subscribers. Each subscriber has a Subscriber ID, Name, and Phone Number. Each plan has a Plan ID, Name, and Monthly Fee. A subscriber can subscribe to many plans and a plan can have many subscribers; for each subscription the Start Date is recorded.

A project management tool tracks projects and the tasks within them. Each project has a Project ID, Name, and Deadline. Each task has a Task ID, Title, Status, and Due Date, and belongs to exactly one project. A project can have many tasks.

A restaurant records customer orders of menu items. Each menu item has an Item ID, Name, and Price. Each order has an Order ID, Order Time, and Table Number. An order can include many menu items and a menu item can appear on many orders; for each item on an order the Quantity is recorded.

A logistics firm manages a fleet of vehicles and their drivers. Each vehicle has a Vehicle ID, Plate Number, and Type. Each driver has a Driver ID, Name, and License Number. A trip has a Trip ID, Start Time, End Time, Origin, and Destination; each trip uses one vehicle driven by one driver.

A manufacturer assembles products from parts. Each product has a Product ID, Name, and List Price. Each part has a Part ID, Name, and Unit Cost. A product is made of many parts and a part can be used in many products; for each part used in a product the Quantity Required is recorded.

An event platform manages events and attendee registrations. Each event has an Event ID, Title, Venue, and Date. Each attendee has an Attendee ID, Name, and Email. An attendee can register for many events and an event can have many attendees; for each registration the Registration Date is recorded.
